newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Pemex denies barrage of Greenpeace charges.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Pemex denies barrage of Greenpeace charges.

text.p: Mexico's state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) on Thursday rejected Greenpeace charges that it was damaging the ecosystem along the Gulf of Mexico coast.

The environmental group has charged that Pemex leaks crude oil through abandoned drilling platforms. Its Rainbow Warrior ship began a tour of the coastline on Monday to study the environmental effect of Pemex's activities.
But Pemex spokeman Juan Saldana denied the charge, calling the accusation "an absolute lie."
"We think we share common objectives in investing in preservation of the ecosystem," Saldana said. "We repect Greenpeace's work."

The environmental group also slammed the oil giant for negligence in maintenance and upkeep in the state of Tabasco. Volunteers plastered "Made by Pemex" signs on the remains of houses that Greenpeace said were destroyed in a February 1995 explosion that killed seven people.
The organization called Pemex's maze of ducts in the region "devil's traps."
On Saturday, Greenpeace workers threw buckets of oil, contaminated water and dead animals at a Pemex building in the port city of Veracruz to protest an oil spill in the region.
Pemex confirmed a 264-gallon (1,000-liter) oil spill, but denied charges of environmental damage.
Local environmental groups charged Pemex with covering up the damage and said the spill was polluting the Tecolutla River, rich in fish, freshwater crabs, oysters and shrimp.
